name: Multifocal Sporadic Venous Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Multifocal Sporadic Venous Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of multiple venous malformations in two or more distinct anatomical sites
No family history of venous malformations or related vascular anomalies
Radiologic confirmation of venous malformations by MRI or ultrasound showing characteristic slow-flow vascular lesions
Exclusion of other combined or syndromic vascular malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multifocal venous malformations confirmed by imaging with no family history of vascular anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is typically negative; diagnosis is clinical and radiologic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple bluish compressible subcutaneous venous malformations
searchTerms: multiple blue soft vein lumps under skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pain exacerbated by dependent positioning or trauma at lesion sites

common.symptomName: Localized soft tissue swelling at affected sites
searchTerms: soft tissue lumps at affected sites

common.symptomName: Venous engorgement visible on physical examination
Functional impairment or limited range of motion near lesions

searchTerms: skin color changes over vein malformations

occasional.symptomName: Recurrent spontaneous bleeding from superficial lesions

searchTerms: painful muscle spasms adjacent to malformations

occasional.symptomName: Edema distal to large venous malformations

rare.symptomName: Deep venous thrombosis associated with extensive malformations
searchTerms: deep vein clots with large malformations

rare.symptomName: Nerve compression symptoms due to lesion expansion
searchTerms: tingling or numbness from mass effect

laboratory: Normal coagulation profile unless thrombophlebitis present
Possible mild elevation of D-dimer in thrombosis
imaging: MRI showing slow-flow venous malformations with characteristic hyperintense T2 signal
Doppler ultrasound demonstrating compressible, low-flow venous channels
Phlebography may show dilated venous lakes without arterial involvement
other: Histopathology shows dilated, thin-walled venous channels without arterial components

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cutaneous and gastrointestinal venous malformations
Often associated with chronic bleeding and anemia
Presence of glomus cells on histology
Often familial with autosomal dominant inheritance
Malignant vascular tumor with spindle cells
Lesions are often violaceous plaques or nodules

redFlags: Signs of deep venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism
